messages.author: c21e804e07c5e732
messages.subject: Re: multiple silhouette plots
parts:
See the example below. It would be convenient if the sd value could be
label in each pair of figures.

library(cluster)
png('main.png',width=1000,height=1000)
par(mfrow=c(3,4))
lapply(
seq(0,1,0.2)
, function(sd) {
x=rbind(
cbind(
rnorm(10,0,sd)
, rnorm(10,0,sd)
, rnorm(10,0,sd)
)
, cbind(
rnorm(15,5,sd)
, rnorm(15,5,sd)
, rnorm(15,5,sd)
)
)
plot(pam(x, 2))
}
)
dev.off()

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: multiple silhouette plots
parts:
Use str to look at the output from the pam function. This should get
you started:

data_gen <- function(sd) {
matrix(rnorm(75 * 2, rep(c(0, 5), c(30, 45), sd = sd)), ncol = 2)
}

library(cluster)
p <- pam(data_gen(0.1), 2)

p$silinfo


Hadley
